plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.

conservative.read: This conservative approach targets a modest ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and high concentration, but also limits upside potential.

balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for ~2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall concentration and leverage while adding a high-quality setup, balancing growth potential with controlled drawdown.

aggressive.read: This aggressive approach targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk due to higher leverage and concentration in volatile assets. Strict stop discipline is critical, as leveraged ETFs decay daily and can lead to rapid losses.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing exposure to income-generating ETFs.
Sell QQQ, CRWD, and SMH to reduce growth-oriented and high-beta exposure.

income.read: This income approach targets ~1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth by rotating into income-focused ETFs and reducing high-beta assets. Distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
